title_en: Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong v. Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Xia Changjun, and Chongqing Aokang Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. According to Article 24 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Contracts on the Right to Use State-owned Land, where a contract for cooperative development of real estate stipulates that the party providing the right to use land does not bear operational risks and only receives fixed benefits, the contract shall be characterized as a contract for transfer of the right to use land. The name given by the parties to the contract shall not affect the determination of the nature of the contract.

full_text_en:
Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong v. Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Xia Changjun, and Chongqing Aokang Real Estate Co., Ltd. — contract dispute case

【Ruling Summary】

I. Pursuant to Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Trial of Disputes over Contracts Involving State-owned Land Use Rights, where a cooperative real estate development contract stipulates that the party providing the land use rights does not bear operational risks but only receives fixed benefits, the contract shall be deemed as a contract for the assignment of land use rights. The name of the contract agreed upon by the parties does not affect the determination of the nature of the contract.

II. Article 52 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract shall be void under any of the following circumstances: ... (2) malicious collusion causing damage to the interests of the State, a collective, or a third party; ..." In accordance with the foregoing provision, where a legal person colludes maliciously with another party to enter into a contract, which on the surface damages the legal person's own interests but in essence damages the interests of a third party, the third party has the right to file a lawsuit to confirm the voidness of the contract.

III. In determining whether "malicious collusion" exists as referred to in the aforementioned provision, it is necessary to analyze whether the parties to the contract have subjective malice, and to comprehensively analyze the specific circumstances at the time of entering into the contract, the content of the contract, and the performance of the contract, so as to make a comprehensive judgment on this basis.

Supreme People's Court Civil Ruling

(2009) Min Shen Zi No. 1760

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at: 6th Floor, New Century Plaza, Yangxin Street, Bicheng Subdistrict, Bishan County, Chongqing.

Legal Representative: Xia Changjun, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Xinzhou, Attorney at Beijing Jiacheng Taihe Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Xia Changjun, male, born on April 5, 1969, Han ethnicity, Chairman of Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., residing at: Unit 6-2, Building 1, No. 20 Yanghe North Road, Yubei District, Chongqing.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Xinzhou, Attorney at Beijing Jiacheng Taihe Law Firm.

Applicant for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Chongqing Aokang Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Building 1, No. 498 Jinjian Road, Bicheng Subdistrict, Bishan County, Chongqing.

Legal Representative: Wang Zhentao, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Jinyan, male, born on August 14, 1979, Han ethnicity, residing at: Dormitory for Teaching Staff of Wenzhou Normal College, Xueyuan East Road, Puxie Street, Lucheng District, Wenzhou City, Zhejiang Province.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Chen Quan, male, born on October 8, 1964, Han ethnicity, residing at: Unit 3-1, Building 2, Unit 3, No. 44 Donglin Avenue, Bishan County, Chongqing.

Agent ad litem: Liu Mou, Attorney at Chongqing Jize Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Meijun, Attorney at Chongqing Jize Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Pi Zhiyong, male, born on August 8, 1968, Han ethnicity, residing at: No. 3-1, No. 10 Nongshi Street, Bishan County, Chongqing.

Agent ad litem: Liu Mou, Attorney at Chongqing Jize Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Meijun, Attorney at Chongqing Jize Law Firm.

The applicants for retrial, Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Bibo Company), Xia Changjun, and Chongqing Aokang Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Aokang Company), being dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2009) Yu Gao Fa Min Zhong Zi No. 141 rendered by the Chongqing High People's Court in the case of dispute over cooperative real estate development contract with the respondents Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong, applied to this Court for retrial. This Court formed a collegiate panel in accordance with the law to examine this case, and the examination has now been concluded.

Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: (I) The judgment of the second instance erred in determining that the legal relationship between Bibo Company and Aokang Company was a transfer of land use rights, lacking factual basis and legal grounds. 1. The "Contract for Joint Development and Construction of Supporting Residential Community for Shoe Capital Industrial Park" (hereinafter referred to as the Joint Development Contract) and the "Exclusive Sales Agreement for Joint Development and Construction of Commercial Residential Community in Shoe Capital Industrial Park" (hereinafter referred to as the Exclusive Sales Agreement) signed between Bibo Company and Aokang Company did not involve any transfer of land use rights. 2. During the joint development, Aokang Company, in addition to contributing the land use rights, also undertook responsibilities such as providing approval documents, handling relevant procedures, coordinating and implementing preferential policies, participating in project supervision, and reviewing and signing project-related external documents. By the end of 2007 when the parties terminated the contract, Aokang Company had incurred expenses of over RMB 40 million for the project. 3. Aokang Company's entrustment of Bibo Company to exclusively sell the 18,000 square meters of housing allocated to Aokang Company was unrelated to whether Aokang Company bore the risks of the cooperative real estate development project. Since the cooperative real estate development project between Aokang Company and Bibo Company was carried out in the name of Aokang Company, Aokang Company still had to legally assume all responsibilities for the project externally. (II) The appraisal conclusion entrusted by the court of second instance to an appraisal institution was procedurally illegal and should not be used as a basis for finding facts. 1. The court of second instance should not have ordered a new appraisal. 2. The appraisal procedure in the second instance was illegal, depriving the parties of their right to choose the appraisal institution. 3. The content of the appraisal was incomplete and insufficient to confirm or exclude the authenticity of the "Receipt for Payment." 4. The second-instance judgment's inference, based on the appraisal conclusion, that Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong had not yet recovered their investment lacked evidentiary support. (III) In accordance with the principle of privity of contract, Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong were not signatories to or obligees/obligors under the "Agreement on Termination of the 'Joint Development of Aokang Residential Community Contract' and 'Exclusive Sales Agreement'" (hereinafter referred to as the Termination Agreement) between Aokang Company and Bibo Company. The second-instance judgment's finding that the Termination Agreement infringed upon the rights and interests of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong lacked legal basis. (IV) The second-instance judgment's finding that Bibo Company and Aokang Company engaged in malicious collusion lacked evidentiary support. 1. Malicious collusion requires knowing or should-know that the interests of a third party are being harmed as a constituent element. At the time of signing the Termination Agreement, Aokang Company was unaware of the "Shareholder Cooperation Agreement" between Chen Quan, Pi Zhiyong, and Xia Changjun. Even if Aokang Company had knowledge of the partnership between Chen Quan, Pi Zhiyong, and Xia Changjun, based on the earlier "Receipt for Payment," Aokang Company had reason to believe that the partnership had been dissolved, and its signing of the Termination Agreement with Bibo Company did not constitute malicious collusion. 2. The second-instance judgment's finding that, based on the overall "rising prices and volumes" trend in the Chongqing commercial housing market at the time of signing the Termination Agreement, the signing of the Termination Agreement by Bibo Company and Aokang Company clearly violated commercial principles, cannot be sustained. 3. The second-instance judgment's finding that Aokang Company paid RMB 3 million in liquidated damages, and that Bibo Company and Aokang Company did not settle debts upon terminating the contract, was contrary to common sense and lacked factual basis. 4. The second-instance judgment's finding that, after the Termination Agreement was signed, Xia Changjun continued to preside over the project work, which was clearly inconsistent with the consequences that should follow from contract termination, lacked factual basis. After the termination agreement was performed, based on Xia Changjun's familiarity with the real estate development project, Aokang Company hired Xia Changjun as one of the project leaders to continue presiding over the project work. (V) The parties in this case are not proper. In a partnership dispute, Aokang Company is not a proper defendant. In the lawsuit concerning the cooperative real estate development dispute between Bibo Company and Aokang Company, Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong are not parties to the contractual relationship and are not proper plaintiffs. Pi Zhiyong is not a shareholder of Bibo Company and has no right to bring a shareholder derivative lawsuit. In summary, the application for retrial is made under Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong submitted a written opinion arguing that: (I) The second-instance judgment correctly found that the legal relationship between Bibo Company and Aokang Company was a transfer of land use rights. 1. Pursuant to Articles 14 and 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Trial of Disputes over Contracts Involving State-owned Land Use Rights, the Joint Development Contract and Exclusive Sales Agreement signed between Bibo Company and Aokang Company provided that Aokang Company would receive a fixed "housing exclusive sales payment" of RMB 19.8 million, which falls under the situation of being a land transfer contract in the guise of a joint construction. 2. The claim by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that Aokang Company had paid expenses of over RMB 40 million for the project is unsupported by evidence. (II) The appraisal conclusion entrusted by the court of second instance was lawful, but the object of the appraisal, the "Receipt for Payment," was not a key piece of evidence in this case. 1. The decision of the court of second instance to order a new appraisal was correct. The selection of the appraisal institution in the second instance was the result of consensus between the parties. 2. The "Receipt for Payment" was isolated evidence, and Bibo Company failed to produce evidence of the source of funds and the channel for refunding the investment. 3. The "Receipt for Payment" contradicts other evidence in this case. 4. The "Receipt for Payment" only proves that Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong returned the investment on December 26, 2006, and cannot be used to infer that the three had dissolved the "Shareholder Cooperation Agreement" based on the return of investment. (III) The malicious collusion between Xia Changjun and Aokang Company is clearly established. Bibo Company and Aokang Company made no capital contribution. Aokang Company, knowing that Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong were the actual investors and controllers of the project, signed the Termination Agreement with Bibo Company, infringing upon the rights and interests of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong. Before the Termination Agreement was signed between Bibo Company and Aokang Company, the project had entered the return on investment period, making it unreasonable to sign the termination agreement at that time. After the contract was terminated, Xia Changjun remained the de facto controller of the project. (IV) There is no issue of improper parties in this case. The retrial application of Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company lacks factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

This Court held that: (I) Regarding the nature of the legal relationship between Bibo Company and Aokang Company. On August 29, 2006, Aokang Company and Bibo Company signed the Joint Development Contract and the Exclusive Sales Agreement. The core content was: Aokang Company and Bibo Company would jointly develop the supporting residential community for the Shoe Capital Industrial Park; Aokang Company would contribute the land as its investment in the joint development, and Bibo Company would be responsible for investing the construction funds required for the project; Aokang Company would not participate in the specific daily affairs of project construction and marketing; the project would maintain independent accounts and independent accounting, managed by Bibo Company on a daily basis, and separate from any other business of either Aokang Company or Bibo Company; any other claims and debts of Aokang Company or Bibo Company would be irrelevant to this project; Aokang Company would receive 18,000 square meters of housing in the project, and all other assets of the joint development project would belong to Bibo Company; Aokang Company would value the 18,000 square meters of housing allocated under the Joint Development Contract at a total price of RMB 19.8 million and entrust Bibo Company with exclusive sales thereof. On March 21, 2007, Aokang Company, Bibo Company, and Xia Changjun signed a "Supplemental Agreement," stipulating: The establishment of a project department in the name of Aokang Company, which would maintain separate accounts and independent accounting; Aokang Company would engrave two seals, "Aokang · Bibo Waterfront Project Department" and "Aokang · Bibo Waterfront Project Department Financial Seal," to be used for all activities of the project. These seals would be under the control of Bibo Company and Xia Changjun, and all economic and legal liabilities arising from documents bearing these seals would be borne by Bibo Company and Xia Changjun. Article 4 of that agreement further provided that Bibo Company and Xia Changjun would be jointly and severally liable for all liabilities and expenses incurred in the development process carried out in the name of Aokang Company, and any losses caused to Aokang Company would be compensated jointly and severally by Bibo Company and Xia Changjun. These provisions indicate that Aokang Company's main obligations in the joint development with Bibo Company were to provide the land and handle relevant procedures; the benefits allocated to Aokang Company were the exclusive sales proceeds of RMB 19.8 million for the 18,000 square meters of housing; and Aokang Company did not bear operational risks. This is consistent with Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Trial of Disputes over Contracts Involving State-owned Land Use Rights, which provides: "Where a cooperative real estate development contract stipulates that the party providing the land use rights does not bear operational risks but only receives fixed benefits, the contract shall be deemed as a contract for the assignment of land use rights." Aokang Company claimed that it had paid over RMB 40 million in expenses for the project and provided copies of some documents, including payments to construction companies. This Court holds: Since the entire project was developed in the name of Aokang Company, external payments for construction works would also be made in the name of Aokang Company. Moreover, most of the document copies presented by Aokang Company bore dates from 2008 and 2009, while the Termination Agreement in this case was signed on December 28, 2007. In the examination procedure of this Court, this is insufficient to prove Aokang Company's claim that it invested over RMB 40 million during its cooperation with Bibo Company. Aokang Company argued that because the project was developed in its name, it was legally responsible for all liabilities arising from the project externally. This Court holds: According to the Supplemental Agreement, although the project department was established in the name of Aokang Company, it maintained separate accounts and independent accounting, and all economic and legal liabilities arising from the project department's operational activities were to be borne by Bibo Company and Xia Changjun. Even if Aokang Company assumed external liability for the project's operational activities, it could still claim from Bibo Company and Xia Changjun joint and several compensation for losses. Therefore, the second-instance judgment's finding that Aokang Company did not bear operational risks was not improper. In summary, the claim by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that the second-instance judgment's characterization of the legal relationship between Aokang Company and Bibo Company as a land use rights transfer contract lacked factual and legal basis cannot be sustained.

(II) Whether the appraisal conclusion entrusted by the court of second instance should be admitted into evidence, and whether the "Receipt for Payment" is sufficient to prove that the partnership among Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong had been dissolved. 1. Whether the decision of the court of second instance to order a new appraisal was correct. Upon reviewing the case file, the "Record of Selection of Appraisal Institution" from the court of first instance indicated that the parties' method of selection was "negotiation," and the selected institution was Chongqing Fazheng Judicial Appraisal Institute. The signatures of the parties included only those of Bibo Company's agent Chen Bing and Xia Changjun's agent Liao Dongfeng, with no signatures of Chen Quan, Pi Zhiyong, or their agents. In the case of selecting an appraisal institution by mutual agreement, the absence of signatures from one party constitutes a procedural defect in the appraisal, and the resulting appraisal conclusion cannot be used as evidence to find facts. The court of second instance's decision to order a new appraisal was not improper. 2. Whether the procedure for entrusting the appraisal in the second instance was lawful. Upon reviewing the case file, the record of June 30, 2009, stated that staff from the judicial appraisal department of the court of second instance informed the parties that the two institutions capable of conducting handwriting formation time appraisal were the appraisal institutions under the Ministry of Public Security and the Judicial Appraisal Center of Southwest University of Political Science and Law. The record of July 2, 2009, stated that staff from the judicial appraisal department informed both parties: "Today we will draw lots to determine the order. If the first-choice institution cannot do it, we will go to the second." The parties all agreed, and on that day, the draw selected the institution under the Ministry of Public Security. The record of July 20, 2009, stated that staff from the judicial appraisal department informed the parties that the selected institution under the Ministry of Public Security did not have the appraisal qualification, and all parties agreed to consult the Judicial Appraisal Center of Southwest University of Political Science and Law to determine if it could conduct the handwriting formation time appraisal. The "Record of Selection of Appraisal Institution by Chongqing High People's Court" dated July 21, 2009, stated that staff from the judicial appraisal department asked the parties whether they agreed to select the Judicial Appraisal Center of Southwest University of Political Science and Law as the appraisal institution, and all parties agreed and signed to confirm. Based on the circumstances recorded in the above minutes, although there were disputes during the selection process, the parties ultimately unanimously agreed to select the Judicial Appraisal Center of Southwest University of Political Science and Law for the appraisal. Therefore, the claim by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that the procedure for selecting the appraisal institution in the second instance was unlawful and effectively deprived the parties of their right to choose the appraisal institution is difficult to sustain, and this Court does not accept it. 3. Whether the scope of the appraisal entrusted by the court of second instance was sufficient to exclude the authenticity of the "Receipt for Payment." The scope of the appraisal entrusted by the court of second instance was: (1) whether the handwriting on Receipts for Payment 1 and 2 was directly written; (2) whether the signature of the payee "Pi Zhiyong" on Receipt for Payment 1 was written by Pi Zhiyong; (3) whether the signature of the payee "Chen Quan" on Receipt for Payment 2 was written by Chen Quan; (4) the time when the signatures of the payees "Pi Zhiyong" and "Chen Quan" were written. Although the above scope did not include the "reason or purpose" and "amount" columns on the receipts where "return of investment" and the corresponding amount in figures and words were written, nor the confirmation signatures and dates of "Chen Quan" in the upper right corners of the two receipts, for the "Receipt for Payment" itself, the most important aspect is the authenticity of the signatures in the "payee" column. Whether other parts are examined does not fundamentally affect the determination of the authenticity of the receipt. Therefore, the claim by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that the scope of the judicial appraisal was incomplete and insufficient to confirm or exclude the authenticity of the "Receipt for Payment" is difficult to sustain, and this Court does not accept it. As Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company failed to provide sufficient evidence to show that the appraisal conclusion entrusted by the court of second instance required a new appraisal, the court of second instance's refusal to grant their application for a new appraisal was not improper. 4. Whether the "Receipt for Payment" is sufficient to prove that the partnership among Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong had been dissolved. The two "Receipts for Payment" indicated "return of investment" in amounts of RMB 1.5 million and RMB 3.65 million, totaling RMB 5.15 million. As the paying entity, Bibo Company did not provide payment evidence to prove that it had actually refunded the RMB 5.15 million investment to Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong. Therefore, the "Receipt for Payment" alone is insufficient to prove that the investments of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong had actually been returned. When Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong established the partnership, they signed a "Shareholder Cooperation Agreement," which detailed the project's basic information, cooperation methods, share allocation, capital contribution time, project management, profit distribution, and risk bearing. If the three negotiated to dissolve the partnership, there should be corresponding evidence of dissolution, settlement of partnership claims and debts, and distribution of partnership profits. Now, relying only on the "Receipt for Payment" to claim that the partnership had been dissolved lacks sufficient evidence. Therefore, even if the signatures of the payees on the "Receipt for Payment" and the signature of "Chen Quan" in the upper right corner were indeed written by Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong, and even if Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong had actually recovered their investments, it is difficult to form sufficient evidence to prove that the partnership among Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong had been dissolved.

(3) Whether the second instance judgment correctly found that the execution of the rescission agreement between Bibo Company and Aokang Company infringed upon the rights of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong. The basic legal relationship in this case is that Xia Changjun, Chen Quan, and Pi Zhiyong invested funds in Bibo Company, and Bibo Company entered into a Joint Development Contract with Aokang Company to carry out project development. On the premise that the partnership relationship among the three individuals continued to exist, Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong could, based on their investment acts, assert against Bibo Company the right to revenue from the project profits. After Bibo Company and Aokang Company entered into the rescission agreement, the project proceeds were attributed to Aokang Company. Because Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong had no investment relationship with Aokang Company, they could not assert claims for project proceeds against Aokang Company. Therefore, the court of second instance held that the act of Bibo Company and Aokang Company entering into the rescission agreement infringed upon the rights of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong, and such finding was not improper. The determination of whether the rescission agreement infringed upon the rights of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong pertains to the issue of whether a tort was established, and does not involve the principle of privity of contract. The assertion by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that, under the principle of privity of contract, the second instance judgment's finding that Chen Quan's and Pi Zhiyong's rights were infringed had no legal basis, cannot be upheld.

(4) Whether there was sufficient evidence to prove the existence of malicious collusion between Aokang Company and Bibo Company as found by the second instance judgment. 1. Regarding the issue of whether Aokang Company knew or should have known that the rescission agreement infringed upon the rights of Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong. The establishment of malicious collusion indeed requires that the actor knew or should have known that such act would harm the interests of the state, the collective, or a third party, meaning the actor had subjective malice. Determining whether the actor had subjective malice must be comprehensively evaluated in light of the specific circumstances of the case. The second instance judgment in this case, based on the specific circumstances at the time of and after the signing of the rescission agreement between Aokang Company and Bibo Company, and in light of the terms and performance of the Shareholder Cooperation Agreement, the Joint Development Contract, and the Underwriting Agreement, comprehensively evaluated whether Aokang Company and Bibo Company constituted malicious collusion. Its method of proof was not improper. 2. According to the facts found, at the time Bibo Company and Aokang Company signed the rescission agreement on December 28, 2007, part of the project's buildings had already been completed, and pre-sale permits had been obtained for the vast majority of the buildings. When the project was about to generate expected profits, Bibo Company and Aokang Company entered into a rescission agreement where only Aokang Company paid 3 million yuan in liquidated damages, assigning the project to Aokang Company. This lacked a reasonable justification for terminating the contract and was indeed an obvious violation of commercial norms. The second instance judgment's finding in this regard was not improper. 3. The nature of the Joint Development Contract and the Underwriting Agreement was a land use right transfer contract. Aokang Company had actually delivered the land to Bibo Company for development, fulfilling its main contractual obligations without any obvious breach of contract. Yet the rescission agreement stipulated that Aokang Company would pay 3 million yuan in liquidated damages to Bibo Company, which was indeed inconsistent with the facts of performance and common sense. The second instance judgment's finding in this regard was not improper. 4. According to the facts found, after the rescission agreement was signed, Xia Changjun remained in full charge of the project. Aokang Company now asserts that Xia Changjun was hired by Aokang Company as the project manager, but given Xia Changjun's special status as the legal representative of Bibo Company and one of the partners, this assertion by Aokang Company is insufficient to overturn the second instance judgment's finding that the conduct of Aokang Company and Xia Changjun after the rescission agreement was signed was clearly inconsistent with the consequences that should have resulted from the contract rescission. In summary, the reasons and evidence relied upon by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company to assert that there was no malicious collusion between Bibo Company and Aokang Company are insufficient to overturn the second instance judgment's finding that malicious collusion existed between Bibo Company and Aokang Company. This assertion cannot be upheld.

(5) Whether there is an issue of improper parties in this case. In this case, Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong filed a lawsuit seeking confirmation that the rescission agreement was void on the grounds that the rescission agreement between Bibo Company and Aokang Company infringed upon their rights. The subject matter of the lawsuit is the tort legal relationship, which does not involve the principle of privity of contract, and is unrelated to whether they were parties to the Joint Development Contract or the rescission agreement. Chen Quan and Pi Zhiyong are one party to the tort legal relationship in this case, meeting the condition for filing a lawsuit stipulated in Article 108, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law, i.e., "the plaintiff has a direct interest in the case," and they are proper plaintiffs in this case. Aokang Company is also a party to the tort legal relationship and is a proper defendant in this case. The assertion by Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company that the parties in this case are improper cannot be upheld.

In conclusion, the retrial applications of Bibo Company, Xia Changjun, and Aokang Company do not meet the circumstances stipulated in Article 179, paragraph 1, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is hereby ordered as follows:

The retrial applications of Chongqing Bibo Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., Xia Changjun, and Chongqing Aokang Real Estate Co., Ltd. are dismissed.
